title: The Sixth Voyage of Sindbad (मराठी)
full_text:
Sindbad narrated his sixth voyage:

'Restlessness seized my soul again, and I set sail on a sixth voyage. Our ship was driven by treacherous currents onto the black granite cliffs of Serendib—the island of Ceylon. The ship shattered, and the surviving crew gathered on a narrow beach at the foot of sheer, impassable mountains.

The beach was strewn with wreckage of centuries, with mountains of ambergris and precious rubies, but there was neither game nor edible herbs. One by one, my companions died of hunger until I stood alone.

Observing that a swift river flowed out from the rocks and plunged into a dark, subterranean cavern beneath the mountain, I reasoned: 'This river must emerge into the open light somewhere; it is better to trust the dark water than to starve upon these rocks!'

I built a sturdy raft of camphor wood, lashed my chests of rubies and ambergris to it, mounted the raft, and steered directly into the subterranean cavern.

For three days and nights, the raft rushed through total darkness beneath the roots of the mountains, scraped by low stalactites. I fell into a swoon.

When I opened my eyes, the sun was shining! The raft was floating in a peaceful, cultivated plain, surrounded by kindly people who conducted me to their capital.

I was brought before the King of Serendib, who was enthroned on a seat of rubies. The king was so delighted by my account of the Caliph Harun al-Rashid and the civilization of Baghdad that he loaded my ship with gifts: a cup of ruby filled with pearls, a bed of snake-skin whose touch wards off disease, and a letter of peace to the Caliph.

I returned to Baghdad as an imperial ambassador, receiving the highest honors from Harun al-Rashid.'
moral: When all earthly ways are blocked, trust the subterranean currents of destiny to carry you to royal honor. [MR]
